text:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a sustained spike in JSON ingest costs for EU regions after the recent model rollout. Looks like sampling didn't apply to a subset of cached prefixes.
jon: Oh, which pipeline? ingest-json-v2 or the legacy collector?
kevin: ingest-json-v2. Some namespaces were missing the region override when we bumped schema to v1.9.
sara: I noticed a bunch of eu-west traces with full payloads instead of sampled summaries. That likely explains the cost delta and the extra egress.
maria: Correct. Also legal flagged that a few logs contain PII fields that our redaction hook didn't catch because of a field rename in the new schema.
ingrid: Can we freeze the rollout and patch the sampling map? I don't want us sending raw emails/phones to downstream systems.
kevin: We can hotfix: revert region_default => region_override mapping and enable the per-region sampler for eu and apac. Quick patch I tested locally:
```
# patch
ingest.pipeline.samplers.region_override = {
  "eu": "1/20",
  "apac": "1/30",
  "default": "1/100"
}
```
jon: If we roll that, what's the deploy surface? Just the collector config and the redaction lambda? ops-bot: deploy triggered for manifest: ingest-json-v2/2026-03-18-02 - status: queued
sara: Also need schema v1.9 -> v2.0 announcement so consumers can stop relying on the old field names. We'll add a compatibility shim that maps old_field -> canonical_field for redaction.
maria: Legal, does that compatibility shim satisfy the PII review or do you want a manual audit of historical logs that might have leaked?
legal: Quick answer — shim + immediate re-redaction for the last 72 hours should be fine as a mitigator. We'll need a followup ticket to run a broader scan and to document the mapping. Please include sample hashes, not raw values, in the report.
kevin: I'll run a reprocess job that writes back sanitized copies and emit a short report. ETA ~2 hours post-patch.
jon: On the observability side, our Prometheus scrape on gpu-fleet-exporter hit a 15s max scrape latency during the spike — that messed up the GPU utilization panels and caused noisy alerts.
sara: Right — dashboards showed nodeCPU spiking but it was actually scrape timeouts. We should tune scrape_interval for that exporter and increase scrape timeout to 20s as a temporary mitigation.
ingrid: Can we silence the noisy alert rule gpu_node_cpu_anomaly for eu until we stabilize? Maybe set the for: to 10m and require both cpu AND gpu_mem anomalies.
maria: Good call. Let's do a short silence for eu alerts and add dependency on scrape_latency < 10s to avoid false positives.
kevin: Plan summary:
1) Patch ingest config (region samplers) — immediate (rolling restart of collectors)
2) Deploy redaction shim + start 72h reprocess job — kevin
3) Adjust Prometheus scrape timeout and scrape_interval for gpu-fleet-exporter — jon
4) Temporarily tune gpu_node_cpu_anomaly alert and silence eu channel — ingrid
5) Legal to review reprocess report — legal
ops-bot: deploy completed: ingest-json-v2/2026-03-18-02 - status: success
jon: Deploys green. I'll open a follow-up PR to bump exporter scrape_timeout and add a scrape_latency label check to the alert rule.
sara: I added a small dashboard panel showing sampling_rate by region so we can monitor this going forward.
maria: Thanks everyone. After kevin's reprocess, post the report here and I'll work with finance to reconcile the cost delta. :thumbsup:
